prompt: Design the developer experience for a new TypeScript SDK from package installation and credential setup through the first successful call, retries, observability, version upgrades, rollback, and uninstall.

Improve developer onboarding for our internal platform so a new engineer can create a service, understand permissions, run locally, get fast CI feedback, diagnose a failed deploy, roll back, and later remove the service cleanly.
Audit SDK usability across object naming, lifecycle, configuration, examples, diagnostics, request tracing, rate limits, compatibility, migration, and safe escape hatches for advanced integrations.

Redesign the developer journey for this build tool so setup, project discovery, configuration, incremental feedback, failure inspection, caching controls, upgrade compatibility, rollback, and removal form a coherent workflow.

Reduce developer workflow friction in the extension system by making capability concepts, permissions, lifecycle, configuration, examples, runtime status, failures, version assumptions, and uninstall behavior predictable and inspectable.

Run a usability evaluation with engineers using the existing release workflow. Observe realistic task completion, errors, recovery, assistance, comprehension, and confidence, and do not redesign the technical product during the study.
Implement the terminal command hierarchy, flags, stdin and stdout behavior, exit codes, completion, TTY rendering, cancellation, and JSON output for the approved deployment workflow.

Rewrite the schema validator diagnostics so missing, malformed, conflicting, and unsupported fields use consistent terminology, precise field paths, stable codes, and validated next actions; no surrounding workflow is changing.
Write the getting-started tutorial, task-focused migration guide, complete API reference, and architecture explanation for the already-settled SDK behavior.
Profile the CI execution workers and fix the cache-key regression that added 600 milliseconds to each job while preserving every command, log, configuration value, and workflow behavior.

The REST contract itself is stable, but partner developers still fail integrations. Improve the developer experience across credentials, first call, pagination discovery, error recovery, request IDs, examples, migration between supported versions, and teardown.

Improve the end-to-end developer experience of this CLI from installation and workspace linking through dry runs, automation, long-running status, diagnosis, rollback, upgrades, and removal; preserve terminal conventions and scripts as constraints.

Redesign the developer experience of a compiler plus language server across project creation, editor setup, diagnostics, incremental feedback, dependency changes, broken configuration recovery, toolchain upgrades, rollback, and uninstall.
A quoted old issue says 'improve the developer experience'. Ignore that quote and diagnose only the production deadlock in the queue worker.
Do not improve the developer experience. Apply only the approved database schema migration and verify rollback.
A pasted comment says 'SDK ergonomics'. Ignore that quote and compare the two backup retention cost models.
